label: prf:q-exponential-unique
title: Proof of uniqueness of the $q$-exponential grouplike
html:
Assume the ambient counit and q-Jackson derivative are additive, and that the flow equation is rigid: an element fixed by D_q with vanishing counit is zero.

The difference e_1 - e_2 is fixed by D_q, since D_q is additive and each e_i satisfies D_q e_i = e_i; and its counit is \epsilon(e_1) - \epsilon(e_2) = 1 - 1 = 0. Rigidity gives e_1 - e_2 = 0.

Rigidity is where the content sits, and it is stated as a hypothesis rather than discharged. The expected argument is that iterating D_q on a primitive of bounded degree forces every coefficient but the leading one to vanish, and the counit condition kills the constant term — which needs a graded q-shuffle Hopf algebra, since the degree bound is what makes the iteration terminate.
